question.text: Magnetic flux (in weber) in a closed circuit of resistance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> varies with time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mfenced><mi>s</mi></mfenced></math> as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>9</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. The magnitude of the induced current at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mA</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Given that magnetic flux ϕ=8t2-9t+5

According to Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction

emf=-dϕdt=-16t-9

At t=0.25 s

emf=-16×0.25-9=5 V

Current =emf  Resistance =5 V20 Ω

=14 A=10004 mA=250 mA
